root_causes.description: The checkout service exhibits a flat 10000ms p99 server-side latency across the entire incident window while all of its downstream dependencies (cart, payment, email, shipping, currency, product-catalog) remain fast (<50ms). No errors, no CPU/memory stress, and no pod restarts were observed, indicating a fixed ~10s delay in checkout request handling rather than resource saturation or a failing dependency.

evidence.observed_value: checkout p99_latency_ms=10000.000 (mean/p50/p95/p99/max all 10000.000) for entire window; downstream deps: cart=9.8ms, payment=1.98ms, email=47.6ms, shipping=4.85ms, currency=1.98ms, product-catalog=48.9ms
error_rate=0.000 across all services including checkout (no anomaly)
evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate < 0.01 — confirms latency-only fault, not http_abort
no CPU saturation — rules out cpu_stress
stable ~25MB working set — rules out memory_stress

evidence.observed_value: checkout trace 'order-consumed' duration=25976ms, status ok (no error)
checkout trace 'user_checkout_multi' duration=20039ms, status ok; trace search: 20 traces, 0 errors, p95_duration=354735ms
evidence.expected_baseline: checkout traces typically complete in < 1s with 0 errors

evidence.observed_value: [no logs found] — zero error log lines from checkout during window
evidence.expected_baseline: no error logs — consistent with latency-only fault

evidence.observed_value: [no K8s events found] — no OOMKilled, BackOff, or crash events for checkout pods
evidence.expected_baseline: no pod lifecycle events — rules out pod_crash

root_causes.description: Frontend p99 latency is also pinned at 10000ms, but this is propagation from its synchronous dependency on checkout (topology: frontend → checkout), not a frontend fault. Frontend's other dependencies (cart, recommendation, product-catalog, shipping, currency, ad) all remained fast.

evidence.observed_value: frontend p99_latency_ms=10000.000 (identical to checkout); recommendation=4.97ms, ad=1.98ms
evidence.expected_baseline: frontend p99_latency_ms < 500ms; matches checkout's 10s delay via synchronous call chain

evidence.observed_value: checkout request_rate mean=0.108 req/s, max=0.267 req/s — traffic flowing normally through frontend→checkout
evidence.expected_baseline: normal request rate, no traffic drop

root_causes.description: A failing or slow downstream dependency of checkout was considered but is largely ruled out: every checkout dependency (cart, payment, email, shipping, currency, product-catalog, and transitively quote) shows normal sub-50ms p99 latency and zero errors during the window. The 10s delay is contained within checkout's own server spans.

evidence.observed_value: all checkout dependencies normal: cart=9.8ms, payment=1.98ms, email=47.6ms, shipping=4.85ms, currency=1.98ms, product-catalog=48.9ms, quote=1.98ms
evidence.expected_baseline: downstream p99 < 50ms — no downstream latency anomaly to propagate

evidence.observed_value: error_rate=0.000 for all downstream services — no dependency returning errors

remediation_steps: Check for and terminate any active chaos/latency-injection experiment targeting the checkout service (e.g., Gremlin, Litmus, Chaos Toolkit, or a feature-flag-driven delay in flagd), since the flat 10s p99 with no resource/error signals indicates an injected fixed delay.

Review recent deployments, config changes, or feature-flag changes to checkout for accidentally introduced sleeps/timeouts or retry storms, and roll back the last change if correlated with the incident window.
If no injection source is found, restart checkout pods (kubectl rollout restart deployment/checkout -n otel-demo) to clear any stuck in-process state causing the delay.
Add a latency SLO alert on checkout p99 (e.g., > 1s for 2m) and implement a circuit breaker / timeout budget in frontend for checkout calls so a 10s checkout delay does not propagate to end-user p99.
Verify recovery by re-querying checkout p99 latency after remediation and confirming it returns to baseline (< 100ms).
